description: Tooling to keep the idea graph healthy as it accumulates cruft over long autonomous-development runs: duplicates, resolved-but-uncollapsed chains, status drift from the actual code, and vague catch-all parents. The reorganization of subtrees (e.g. the 'UI' catch-all, see 18263fc2) should become a byproduct of this tooling rather than a manual slog. Evidence motivating this: 2a9e3aba and f592b156 are byte-identical duplicates; a05ea545/891e2ee0/855e26a1 are three ideas for one shipped feature; 8ae9e8da/fe0e0aaf/b3f8518f/4e50493a were all already implemented but still marked open.

supportingConnections.hypothesis: Agents create near-duplicates in long runs; a report finds them before the value flow splits between two copies.
Merging keeps links, history and commitments of both ideas, so cleaning duplicates loses nothing.
Suggested parents move ideas out of catch-all containers into the place where their value actually flows.
Open ideas that are already done distort priorities and waste agent time; reconciling against the code removes them.
One hygiene report makes graph decay visible as numbers that can be watched over time.
Parents that name a structural part of the product make placement predictable for agents and humans.
Thresholds tuned to the embedding model keep duplicate reports short enough to act on.
Parent-child pairs are intentional refinements, not duplicates; excluding them removes most false alarms.
A tested core lets the duplicate logic change without breaking the MCP tool and the UI that use it.
Uses cancelled and similar ideas as durable graph memory to prevent noise.
Prevents a class of committedIn/commitments inconsistencies at the source instead of repairing them afterwards.
Invalid states are invisible graph defects; refusing them at the API keeps every status-based rule trustworthy.

status.comment: Container: graph health needs new tools as the graph and its failure modes grow (Felix 2026-10-17: containers can always be filled with ideas).
